home.hero_title: Report Cyber Incidents & Secure Digital Evidence
home.hero_sub: An official platform for citizens to file cybercrime incidents, generate cryptographic evidence baselines, and receive verified investigation tracking.
home.card1_desc: Submit details regarding phishing, scam transfers, identity theft, or extortion. Upload original evidence files for memory-safe SHA-256 fingerprinting.
home.card2_desc: Look up an active case using your assigned CASE-YYYY-XXXXX tracking code to review real-time status updates and cryptographic custody verification.
home.advisory_sub: Follow these critical steps immediately after an incident to ensure your evidence is legally admissible in formal investigations:
home.advisory_tip1_desc: Do not crop, edit, mark, or blur screenshots. Ensure status bars, dates, timestamps, usernames, and profile URLs are fully visible.
home.advisory_tip2_title: Do Not Delete Chat Logs or Messages
home.advisory_tip2_desc: Keep complete conversation histories on messaging apps (Telegram, WhatsApp, Messenger, Viber). Export raw chat logs if supported.
home.advisory_tip3_desc: Save official transaction receipts, bank reference numbers, GCash/Maya reference IDs, and wallet addresses involved in fraudulent transfers.
home.advisory_tip4_desc: Copy full website URLs, phishing domain links, email addresses, and raw email headers whenever available.
home.faq_sub: Essential information regarding reporting security, citizen privacy, and investigative timelines.
home.faq_q1: Can I report anonymously, and is my personal identity protected?
home.faq_a1: Yes. Providing your name and contact details is completely optional. If you choose not to provide personal details, your report will be cataloged under an anonymous classification. All internal case records and public verification lookups strictly redact personal identifiers.
home.faq_q2: How do tracking keys work, and why do I not need an account or password?
home.faq_a2: When you submit an incident, the system generates a unique cryptographic tracking identifier in the format CASE-YYYY-XXXXX. This key acts as your secure bearer token for public status lookups. No personal accounts, passwords, or persistent profiles are required, ensuring zero tracking of citizens.
home.faq_q3: How does cryptographic fingerprinting protect legal admissibility in court?
home.faq_a3: Upon receipt, your uploaded evidence file is passed directly through a native SHA-256 and MD5 cryptographic pipeline. The calculated mathematical hash is permanently timestamped into an append-only Chain of Custody database ledger. In legal proceedings, this establishes mathematical proof that the evidence was not modified, swapped, or tampered with after submission.
home.faq_q4: What happens after I submit, and what are the expected response timelines?
home.faq_a4: Newly submitted incidents enter the "Reported" stage immediately. Within 24 to 48 hours, an authorized digital forensic officer conducts an initial review to evaluate severity, verify artifact integrity, and assign priority. You can monitor each milestone (Reported → Under Review → Investigating → Resolved) in real time using the case tracker.

report.title: File Official Incident Report
report.subtitle: Submit cybercrime details, financial loss statements, and digital evidence. Your evidence will be immediately hashed using SHA-256 and sealed in an append-only custody ledger.
report.anonymous_notice: Anonymous Filing: You do not need an account. Complainant details are strictly optional and confidential.
report.incident_title_placeholder: e.g., Unauthorized GCash Transfer via Fake Bank SMS
report.suspect_hint: Include phone numbers, GCash/bank account numbers, social media handles, or suspicious URLs.
report.desc_placeholder: Describe the incident in detail: how the suspect contacted you, what they claimed, links sent, and any actions taken...
report.dropzone_title: Drop files here or click to browse
report.dropzone_sub: Supported: PNG, JPG, PDF, TXT, CSV, LOG, EML, ZIP (Max 50MB)
report.contact_placeholder: e.g., 0917-xxx-xxxx or email@example.com (used only for investigator follow-up)
report.modal_sub: Your report has been registered and cryptographically sealed. Please save your Tracking Key to monitor case progress.
report.modal_warning: IMPORTANT: Do not lose this tracking key. Because no user accounts are created, this key is the ONLY way to access public case updates.

track.title: Track Incident Status & Custody
track.subtitle: Enter your assigned Tracking ID to inspect real-time review progress, cryptographic evidence verification, and investigation milestones.
track.progress_sub: Understand what each investigation phase means as your report advances through verified review.
track.awaiting_desc: Enter your assigned Tracking Key above or select one of the sample cases to inspect real-time status updates, cryptographic evidence intake, and investigation progress.
track.privacy_note: Public Tracking is strictly read-only and sanitized for citizen privacy.

Reported.name: Reported
Reported.desc: Incident successfully received, hashed with SHA-256, and permanently logged in the intake ledger.

Under Review.name: Under Review
Under Review.desc: An assigned forensic officer is actively reviewing the incident details, verifying evidence integrity, and determining investigative priority.

Investigating.name: Investigating
Investigating.desc: Active forensic examination underway. Officers are analyzing digital artifacts, transaction flows, and suspect indicators.

Resolved.name: Resolved
Resolved.desc: Investigation concluded. Findings, formal evidence dossiers, and incident reports have been prepared for legal handoff or closure.

Closed.name: Closed
Closed.desc: Case formally closed and archived with complete cryptographic Chain of Custody documentation.
